title: Understanding k-fold Cross Validation
text: In k-fold cross-validation, the dataset is divided into k subsets, and the model is trained and validated k times, each time using a different subset as the validation set and the remaining as the training set.

title: Bias and Variance in Cross Validation
text: Increasing k in k-fold cross-validation generally reduces the variance of the model's performance estimate, but how does it affect the bias?

title: Computational Intensity of Cross Validation
text: Consider the computational cost of running k-fold cross-validation compared to a single train-test split. Is cross-validation more or less computationally intensive?

title: Using Entire Dataset in Cross Validation
text: In cross-validation, each data point gets to be in a validation set exactly once and gets to be in a training set k-1 times. How does this compare to using a single train-test split?

title: Cross Validation in Production
text: Think about the purpose of cross-validation during model development. Why might it not be suitable for use in a production environment?
